name: Screwfix
desc: UK multichannel retailer of tools, plumbing, electrical and building supplies for tradespeople, with click-and-collect stores.
ownership: subsidiary of Kingfisher plc (bought 1999)
capacity_detail: Revenue GBP 2,538m in 2023 (Wikipedia infobox, as reported by Kingfisher)
markets: United Kingdom and Ireland, with a store network and online and app ordering for trade customers
rationale: Screwfix targets tradesmen, a heavily male audience that overlaps with F1 viewers; technical, engineering-led positioning suits trackside branding.

name: B&Q
desc: British DIY and home improvement retailer selling tools, garden, kitchen and building products through large stores and online.
ownership: subsidiary of Kingfisher plc (wholly owned)
capacity_detail: Revenue GBP 3.8bn in 2022/23 (Wikipedia infobox)
markets: United Kingdom and Ireland through large-format stores and online home-improvement retail
rationale: Mass-market UK household brand; F1's growing UK family audience and British GP hospitality could support brand-building and customer promotions.

name: Primark
desc: Irish value fashion retailer, trading as Penneys in Ireland, with about 495 stores in 19 countries.
ownership: subsidiary of Associated British Foods (spin-off planned for late 2027)
capacity_detail: Revenue GBP 9,448m in 2024 (Wikipedia infobox)
markets: 19 countries including Ireland, the United Kingdom, continental Europe and the United States
rationale: Primark is expanding in the US and Europe; F1's young, growing fan base and licensed merchandise fit its value fashion offer.

name: Škoda Auto
desc: Czech car manufacturer making Octavia, Superb and electric Enyaq models, wholly owned by Volkswagen Group since 2000.
ownership: subsidiary of Volkswagen Group (100% since May 2000)
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 27.8bn in 2025 (Wikipedia)
markets: Europe, India and other international markets, with rally heritage in the World Rally Championship
rationale: Škoda has long rally heritage and sports-sponsorship habits; as sister brand of Audi F1 it could use group F1 assets.
parent_f1: owner of a current F1 partner (Audi F1 team)

name: SEAT (incl. Cupra)
industry: car manufacturer, SEAT and Cupra brands
desc: Spanish car maker producing SEAT and performance-oriented Cupra brand vehicles, fully owned by the Volkswagen Group.
ownership: subsidiary of Volkswagen Group (fully owned)
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 14.53bn in 2024 (Wikipedia infobox)
markets: Spain, Germany, the UK and other European markets, plus Mexico and Australia for Cupra
rationale: Cupra positions itself as a performance challenger brand with a racing arm; F1 visibility would back its sporty image.
parent_f1: owner of a current F1 partner (Audi F1 team)

name: Bentley Motors
desc: British maker of luxury grand tourers and SUVs, owned by Volkswagen Group since 1998 and managed under Audi.
ownership: subsidiary of Audi, part of Volkswagen Group (owned since 1998)
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 2,650m in 2024 (Wikipedia infobox)
markets: Luxury car buyers in the Americas, China, Europe, the Middle East and Asia-Pacific
rationale: Ultra-luxury buyers match F1 Paddock Club guests; Bentley's Le Mans heritage gives credible motorsport storytelling.
parent_f1: owner of a current F1 partner (Audi F1 team)

name: Automobili Lamborghini
desc: Italian supercar and luxury SUV maker controlled by Audi since 1998, with Squadra Corse racing programmes.
ownership: subsidiary of Audi AG, part of Volkswagen Group (since 1998)
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 3.10bn in 2024 (Wikipedia infobox)
markets: Supercar customers in the Americas, EMEA and Asia-Pacific, with GT3 and Super Trofeo racing
rationale: Supercar brand with endurance-racing programmes; F1 races in key luxury markets offer client hospitality and brand theatre.
parent_f1: owner of a current F1 partner (Audi F1 team)

name: Ducati
desc: Italian premium motorcycle maker and MotoGP factory team, owned by Lamborghini within Audi and Volkswagen Group.
ownership: subsidiary of Automobili Lamborghini, part of Audi / Volkswagen Group (100% voting rights since 2012)
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 925m in 2025 (Wikipedia infobox)
sponsorships: Runs the Ducati Corse factory MotoGP team (champions 2022-2025 per Wikipedia)
markets: Premium motorcycle buyers in Europe, the Americas and Asia-Pacific
rationale: MotoGP-dominant brand with a motorsport fan base; F1 would broaden its premium lifestyle reach among four-wheel enthusiasts.
parent_f1: owner of a current F1 partner (Audi F1 team)

name: Maserati
desc: Italian luxury sports car brand owned by Stellantis, formerly fielding a team in Formula E.
ownership: subsidiary of Stellantis (since 2021 merger)
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 2.3bn in 2023 (Wikipedia infobox)
sponsorships: Maserati MSG Racing in Formula E 2022-2025
markets: Luxury car buyers in North America, Europe, China and the Middle East
rationale: Racing heritage and recent Formula E exit leave budget for premium motorsport; F1 fits its relaunch in luxury markets.

name: Scania
desc: Swedish manufacturer of heavy trucks, buses and engines, wholly owned by Traton within Volkswagen Group.
ownership: subsidiary of Traton, part of Volkswagen Group (100% since 2015)
capacity_detail: Net sales SEK 198.5bn in 2025 (Wikipedia)
markets: Trucks, buses and engines sold in Europe, Latin America, Asia and Africa
rationale: Truck brands sell on engineering and uptime; F1 logistics and B2B hospitality could support Scania's fleet-customer relationships.
parent_f1: owner of a current F1 partner (Volkswagen group (Audi F1 team))

name: Automobile Dacia
desc: Romanian car maker owned by Renault since 1999, producing budget Dacia models sold across Europe.
ownership: subsidiary of Renault Group (bought from Romanian state 1999)
capacity_detail: Revenue RON 29,920m (EUR 5,689m) in 2025 (Wikipedia infobox)
sponsorships: Sponsor of UTMB World Series since 2023; formerly Udinese Calcio (to 2023)
markets: Europe, the Mediterranean and North Africa, with production in Romania and Morocco
rationale: Dacia is a sports-sponsoring value brand whose sister Alpine runs an F1 team, easing group-level activation.
parent_f1: owner of a current F1 partner (Alpine F1 team)

name: Supercell
desc: Finnish mobile game developer behind Clash of Clans, Clash Royale and Brawl Stars, controlled by Tencent.
ownership: subsidiary of Tencent via Halti S.A. consortium (81.4%; Tencent 51.2% of Halti)
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 2.65bn in 2025 (Wikipedia infobox; body text gives USD 3bn for 2024)
markets: Players worldwide on iOS and Android, strongest in North America, Europe and Asia
rationale: Supercell needs young global audiences for Brawl Stars and Clash; F1's Gen-Z growth and esports suit in-game crossovers.
parent_f1: owner of a current F1 partner (PUBG Mobile (publisher))

name: SWISS (Swiss International Air Lines)
desc: Swiss flag carrier flying from Zurich and Geneva to Europe and long-haul destinations, owned by Lufthansa Group.
ownership: subsidiary of Lufthansa Group (takeover completed July 2007)
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 6,481m in 2025 (Wikipedia infobox)
markets: Flights from Switzerland to Europe, North America, Asia, Africa and Latin America
rationale: Premium Swiss airline courting high-yield travellers; F1 hospitality and fly-in packages to European races suit its premium cabins.

name: Brussels Airlines
desc: Belgian flag carrier serving Europe and Africa from Brussels Airport, wholly owned by Lufthansa via SN Airholding.
ownership: subsidiary of Lufthansa Group via SN Airholding (full ownership since January 2017)
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 1,647m in 2025 (Wikipedia infobox)
markets: Flights from Brussels to Europe, Africa and North America
rationale: As home-market airline for the Belgian Grand Prix at Spa, Brussels Airlines could sell race travel packages to fans.

name: Eurowings
desc: German low-cost airline wholly owned by Lufthansa, flying point-to-point routes across Europe from German and other bases.
ownership: subsidiary of Lufthansa Group (wholly owned)
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 3,077m in 2025 (Wikipedia)
sponsorships: Borussia Dortmund (Bundesliga) partner, sponsorship livery noted April 2022 (Wikipedia)
markets: Germany, Austria, Switzerland and leisure destinations across Europe and the Mediterranean
rationale: Already sponsors Bundesliga football; F1 race-weekend travel to European circuits fits its leisure route network.

name: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines
desc: Dutch flag carrier based at Amsterdam Schiphol, operating a global network as part of Air France-KLM.
ownership: subsidiary of Air France-KLM
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 13.2bn in 2025 (Wikipedia infobox)
markets: Global long-haul and European network from Amsterdam Schiphol hub
rationale: Home airline of Max Verstappen's Dutch fan base; F1 fly-in packages and Orange-army marketing fit naturally.

name: Transavia
desc: Dutch low-cost airline wholly owned by KLM, flying leisure routes from the Netherlands within Air France-KLM.
ownership: subsidiary of KLM, part of Air France-KLM (wholly owned)
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 3.452bn in 2025 (Wikipedia financial table)
markets: Leisure and city routes from the Netherlands and France to Europe, North Africa and the Middle East
rationale: Low-cost carrier for Dutch and French fans travelling to European Grands Prix; race-route promotions could lift bookings.

name: Iberia
desc: Spanish flag carrier and Madrid hub airline, strong on Europe-Latin America routes, part of IAG.
ownership: subsidiary of International Airlines Group (IAG)
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 7.54bn in 2024 (Wikipedia infobox; table gives EUR 7.8bn)
markets: Spain, Europe and Latin America from the Madrid hub, plus North America
rationale: Madrid hosts a Grand Prix from 2026; Iberia links Spain to Latin American F1 fans in Mexico and Brazil.

name: Vueling
desc: Barcelona-based low-cost airline flying European routes, 97.52% owned by IAG and run as a standalone company.
ownership: subsidiary of International Airlines Group (97.52%)
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 3,230m in 2025 (Wikipedia business trends table)
markets: Short-haul routes from Barcelona and other Spanish bases across Europe and North Africa
rationale: Main airline at Barcelona, home of the Spanish Grand Prix; race-travel deals could reach European fan flows.

name: British Airways
desc: UK flag carrier operating from London Heathrow and Gatwick to a global network, owned by IAG.
ownership: subsidiary of International Airlines Group (IAG)
capacity_detail: Revenue GBP 14.6bn (Wikipedia infobox; table: GBP 14.5bn 2024, GBP 14.6bn 2025)
sponsorships: Official airline of the Wimbledon Championships
markets: Global network from London to North America, Asia, the Middle East, Africa and Europe
rationale: Premium global airline with Wimbledon precedent; F1's UK teams and global calendar fit BA's premium-traveller marketing.

name: Direct Line Group
desc: UK motor and home insurer selling under Direct Line, Churchill and Green Flag, acquired by Aviva in 2025.
ownership: subsidiary of Aviva (acquisition completed 1 July 2025)
capacity_detail: Bought by Aviva at a price valuing it at GBP 3.70bn; deal agreed Dec 2024, completed 1 July 2025
markets: United Kingdom motor, home, breakdown and pet insurance customers
rationale: Motor insurance and Green Flag breakdown brands speak to drivers; F1's large UK audience suits brand-led motor insurance marketing.

name: esure
desc: UK online motor and home insurer, sold by Bain Capital to Belgian insurer Ageas in 2025.
ownership: subsidiary of Ageas (acquisition completed 30 September 2025)
capacity_detail: Bought by Ageas from Bain Capital for EUR 1.510bn; agreed April 2025, completed 30 Sept 2025
markets: United Kingdom motor and home insurance customers, sold online
rationale: Digital motor insurer needing brand awareness among UK drivers; F1 content and broadcast-adjacent sponsorship could deliver it.

name: TSB Bank
desc: UK high-street retail bank, sold by Sabadell to Santander for GBP 2.65bn in a deal completed April 2026.
ownership: subsidiary of Santander UK, part of Banco Santander (completed 30 April 2026)
capacity_detail: Bought by Santander from Sabadell for GBP 2.65bn; announced 1 July 2025, completed 30 April 2026
markets: United Kingdom retail banking, mortgages and current accounts
rationale: Parent Santander already sponsors F1; TSB could join group activations, though integration into Santander UK may retire the brand.

name: If P&C Insurance
desc: Leading Nordic property and casualty insurer serving private and business customers in Sweden, Norway, Finland and Denmark.
ownership: subsidiary of Sampo Oyj (full ownership since 2004)
capacity_detail: Gross premiums written SEK 87bn in 2025 (Wikipedia, shown as revenue)
markets: Sweden, Norway, Finland, Denmark and the Baltic countries
rationale: Nordic insurer with motor focus; F1 visibility could support If's car insurance brand across four Nordic markets.

name: Atradius
desc: Dutch trade credit insurer, surety and collections provider, the credit insurance arm of Grupo Catalana Occidente.
ownership: subsidiary of Grupo Catalana Occidente (83.20% economic stake, direct and via Grupo CyC)
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 2.6bn in 2025 (Wikipedia)
markets: Trade credit insurance for exporters across Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific and Africa
rationale: B2B insurer serving exporters; F1 hospitality offers a global stage for client entertainment with corporate risk managers.

name: BNL (Banca Nazionale del Lavoro)
desc: Italian commercial bank owned by BNP Paribas since 2006, running the group's retail and corporate banking in Italy.
ownership: subsidiary of BNP Paribas (since 2006; delisted after takeover)
capacity_detail: Main sponsor of the Internazionali BNL d'Italia (Italian Open) tennis tournament in Rome
sponsorships: Title sponsor, Internazionali BNL d'Italia (ATP/WTA Rome)
markets: Retail, private and corporate banking across Italy
rationale: Already a premier tennis sponsor; the Imola and Monza races give BNL a home F1 platform for Italian clients.

name: Telenet
desc: Belgian cable, broadband, TV and mobile operator, fully owned by Liberty Global after its 2023 take-private.
ownership: subsidiary of Liberty Global (100%; delisted from Euronext Brussels October 2023)
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 2,839.6m in 2025 (Wikipedia infobox; citation label may be outdated)
sponsorships: Principal sponsor KV Mechelen; secondary sponsor Club Brugge; title sponsor Telenet UCI Cyclo-cross World Cup
markets: Flanders and Brussels in Belgium, plus Luxembourg, for broadband, TV and mobile
rationale: Telenet already sponsors football and cycling; the Belgian Grand Prix at Spa gives a home F1 stage for its TV and mobile brands.

name: Fastweb
desc: Italian broadband and mobile operator owned by Swisscom, merged with Vodafone Italia on 1 January 2026.
ownership: subsidiary of Swisscom (controlling stake 2007, remaining shares after 2010 tender)
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 2.809bn in 2024 (Wikipedia infobox), before merger with Vodafone Italia
markets: Italy, consumer and business broadband, mobile and enterprise services
rationale: Enlarged Fastweb must build one brand as Vodafone is phased out; Imola and Monza offer Italian F1 visibility.

name: Wind Tre
desc: Italian mobile and fixed-line operator selling under the WINDTRE brand, wholly owned by CK Hutchison since 2018.
ownership: subsidiary of CK Hutchison Holdings (sole shareholder since September 2018)
capacity_detail: Total revenue EUR 3,820m in 2025 (CK Hutchison 2025 annual report, telecom operations review)
markets: Italy, mobile and fixed-line customers, plus energy and insurance add-ons
rationale: Mass-market Italian telecom brand; F1's Italian races and huge Ferrari fan base offer national reach for 5G marketing.

name: British Gas
desc: UK household energy supplier and boiler, heating and home services brand, operated by Centrica subsidiaries.
ownership: subsidiary of Centrica (British Gas Trading Ltd and other Centrica subsidiaries)
capacity_detail: Five-year partnership with the British Olympic Association (Team GB) and ParalympicsGB, from 2023
sponsorships: Team GB and ParalympicsGB partner from 2023; British Swimming 2009-2015
markets: United Kingdom households for gas, electricity, boiler cover and EV charging services
rationale: Large UK consumer brand already investing in Olympic sponsorship; British GP visibility could promote EV charging and home energy.

name: Biedronka
desc: Poland's largest discount grocery chain, owned by Portuguese retailer Jerónimo Martins.
ownership: subsidiary of Jerónimo Martins
capacity_detail: Revenue PLN 102.0bn in 2024 (Wikipedia infobox)
markets: Poland, with a nationwide store network
rationale: Mass Polish grocery brand; F1's growing Central European audience could support loyalty promotions, though reach is domestic.

name: Saint Laurent
desc: Paris luxury fashion house making ready-to-wear, leather goods and shoes, owned by Kering since 1999.
ownership: subsidiary of Kering (bought 1999)
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 2.9bn in 2024; EUR 3.2bn in 2023 (Wikipedia)
markets: Luxury boutiques and wholesale in Europe, North America, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East
rationale: Sister brand Gucci joins Alpine in 2027; Saint Laurent could follow with paddock fashion and Las Vegas or Monaco activations.
parent_f1: current F1 partner or owner of one (Gucci (Alpine))

name: Bottega Veneta
desc: Italian luxury house known for woven leather goods and ready-to-wear, part of the Kering group.
ownership: subsidiary of Kering
capacity_detail: Revenue about EUR 1.7bn in 2024, up from EUR 1.645bn in 2023 (Wikipedia, citing Kering results)
markets: Luxury retail in Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific, Japan and the Middle East
rationale: Quiet-luxury brand targeting wealthy clients; F1's Paddock Club and Monaco audiences match its customer profile.
parent_f1: current F1 partner or owner of one (Gucci (Alpine))

name: Jimmy Choo
desc: London luxury shoe and accessories brand, acquired by Michael Kors (now Capri Holdings) in 2017.
ownership: subsidiary of Capri Holdings via Jimmy Choo Group Limited (acquired November 2017)
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 600m in fiscal 2026 (year to 28 March 2026), USD 605m in fiscal 2025 (Capri 8-K, Schedule 3)
markets: Luxury footwear and bags sold in the Americas, EMEA and Asia
rationale: British luxury brand targeting USD 800m sales; glamorous F1 events like Monaco and Las Vegas suit its red-carpet image.

name: Stone Island
desc: Italian premium sportswear and outerwear brand known for garment-dyeing research, part of the Moncler Group since 2021.
ownership: subsidiary of Moncler (acquisition for EUR 1.15bn completed 31 March 2021)
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 411.2m in 2025 (Wikipedia infobox)
markets: Europe, North America and Asia through flagship stores, wholesale and online
rationale: Cult brand among football and terrace culture fans; F1 merchandise collaborations could extend its technical, performance image.

name: Snaitech (Snai)
desc: Italian omnichannel betting and gaming operator running the Snai brand, acquired by Flutter from Playtech in 2025.
ownership: subsidiary of Flutter Entertainment (acquisition completed April 2025; in International division)
capacity_detail: Acquired by Flutter at an enterprise value of EUR 2.3bn in cash, completed April 2025
markets: Italy, through retail betting shops and online sports betting and gaming
rationale: Snai is one of Italy's best-known betting brands; F1 content suits sports-betting engagement where sponsorship rules allow.
parent_f1: owner of a current F1 partner (FanDuel)

name: Hachette Livre
desc: French book publisher, reported as Lagardère Publishing, with trade, education and partworks imprints across many countries.
ownership: subsidiary of Lagardère SA (since 1981), itself majority-owned by Louis Hachette Group
capacity_detail: Lagardère Publishing revenue EUR 3,001m in 2025 (Louis Hachette Group FY2025 press release)
markets: France, the United Kingdom, the United States, Spain and other markets through publishing imprints
rationale: Publisher with partworks and licensed books; F1 publishing licences and young-reader content could tie into a partnership.

name: Lagardère Travel Retail
desc: French travel retail operator running duty-free, travel essentials and dining outlets in airports and stations worldwide.
ownership: subsidiary of Lagardère SA, majority-owned by Louis Hachette Group
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 6,133m in 2025, up 5.5% (Louis Hachette Group FY2025 press release; Moodie Davitt Report)
markets: Airports and stations in Europe, the Americas, Africa, the Middle East and Asia-Pacific
rationale: Airport retailer reaching affluent travellers; F1 merchandise and race-city airport activations could lift duty-free sales.

name: Fremantle
desc: London-based TV production and distribution company behind global entertainment formats, part of RTL Group since 2000.
ownership: subsidiary of RTL Group (content business), itself majority-owned by Bertelsmann
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 2.04bn in 2025, down 9.4% (Advanced Television, reporting RTL Group results)
markets: Production companies and format sales across Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East
rationale: Global producer seeking premium content; an F1 partnership could support documentary, entertainment and format production deals.

name: Nespresso
desc: Swiss premium coffee-capsule and machine brand run as an operating unit of Nestlé, with boutiques worldwide.
ownership: subsidiary (operating unit) of Nestlé S.A.
capacity_detail: Reported sales CHF 6.5bn in 2025, organic growth 6.0% (Nestlé FY2025 press release)
markets: Boutiques, online and B2B coffee in Europe, North America (strongest growth) and Asia-Pacific
rationale: Premium lifestyle brand growing fast in North America; F1 hospitality and US races suit Nespresso's luxury coffee positioning.
parent_f1: owner of a current F1 partner (KitKat, S.Pellegrino)

name: Fresenius Kabi
desc: German maker of generic intravenous drugs, clinical nutrition, infusion technology and biosimilars, part of Fresenius.
ownership: subsidiary of Fresenius SE & Co. KGaA
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 8,612m in 2025 (Fresenius Annual Report 2025, results of operations)
markets: Hospitals and healthcare providers in Europe, North America, Latin America and Asia-Pacific
rationale: B2B healthcare brand with limited consumer need; F1 would mainly serve employer branding and hospital-client hospitality.

name: Helios Kliniken
desc: Germany's largest private hospital operator, running clinics and outpatient centres as part of Fresenius Helios.
ownership: subsidiary of Fresenius via Fresenius Helios
capacity_detail: Helios Germany revenue EUR 8,121m in 2025 (Fresenius Annual Report 2025)
markets: Germany, hospitals and outpatient care centres nationwide
rationale: Domestic hospital operator; F1 fit is weak beyond medical-partner or employer-branding roles.

name: Quirónsalud
desc: Spain's largest private hospital group, reported by Fresenius as Helios Spain, also operating in Latin America.
ownership: subsidiary of Fresenius via Fresenius Helios (reported as Helios Spain)
capacity_detail: Helios Spain revenue EUR 5,429m in 2025 (Fresenius Annual Report 2025)
markets: Spain, with hospitals in Colombia and Peru
rationale: With a Madrid Grand Prix from 2026, Quirónsalud could serve as a medical partner and raise its premium private-care profile.

name: MAN Truck & Bus
desc: German manufacturer of trucks, buses and vans, a subsidiary of Traton within the Volkswagen Group.
ownership: subsidiary of Traton, part of Volkswagen Group
capacity_detail: Sales revenue EUR 14.1bn in 2025, up 3% (MAN results release reported by Fleet.ie)
markets: Trucks, buses and vans sold across Europe, plus markets in Africa, the Middle East and Asia
rationale: Truck maker selling to fleet operators; F1 logistics showcases and B2B hospitality fit, as sister Audi enters F1.
parent_f1: owner of a current F1 partner (Volkswagen group (Audi F1 team))

name: Brico Dépôt France
desc: French discount DIY and building materials warehouse chain, owned by Kingfisher since 2002, also trading in Iberia.
ownership: subsidiary of Kingfisher plc (acquired with Castorama, 2002)
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 2.24bn for Brico Dépôt France, year ended 31 January 2025 (Wikipedia infobox)
markets: France, with sister chains in Spain and Portugal
rationale: Value DIY retailer for French builders and homeowners; a mainly domestic brand with modest F1 fit.

name: Monoprix
desc: French city-centre retailer selling food, fashion and home goods, fully owned by Casino Group (renamed Plesio).
ownership: subsidiary of Casino Group / Plesio (fully owned since 2013)
capacity_detail: Net sales EUR 4,046m in 2025 (Casino Group Q4 and FY2025 net sales release)
markets: France, especially Paris and large city centres, with Monop' and Naturalia formats
rationale: Urban lifestyle retailer with fashion lines; a domestic brand with limited F1 need, and parent finances are strained.

name: Franprix
desc: French urban convenience supermarket chain, mainly in Paris, operated by Casino Group (renamed Plesio).
ownership: subsidiary of Casino Group / Plesio
capacity_detail: Net sales EUR 1,504m in 2025 (Casino Group Q4 and FY2025 net sales release)
markets: France, chiefly Paris and the Île-de-France region
rationale: Domestic convenience grocer; F1 relevance is low and parent finances are strained.

name: Cdiscount
desc: French e-commerce site and marketplace selling electronics, home and everyday goods, controlled by Casino Group.
ownership: subsidiary of Casino Group / Plesio via Cnova (Casino held 99.6% from 2011)
capacity_detail: Net sales EUR 1,027m in 2025 (Casino Group Q4 and FY2025 net sales release)
markets: France, online direct sales and third-party marketplace
rationale: French online retailer competing with Amazon; F1's young French audience could support brand building, though budgets are tight.

name: MC (Continente)
industry: food retail and health and beauty
desc: Sonae's food retail arm, market leader in Portugal through the Continente brand in hypermarket, supermarket and convenience formats.
ownership: subsidiary of Sonae SGPS
capacity_detail: MC turnover EUR 8.9bn in 2025, up 16% (ESM Magazine; ECO News)
markets: Portugal, with health and beauty chains Druni and Arenal in Spain
rationale: Portugal's leading grocer; F1's Portimão history and Iberian audience offer loyalty-card promotions, but reach is mostly domestic.

name: Worten
desc: Portuguese consumer electronics and appliance retailer with stores and online marketplace in Portugal and Spain, owned by Sonae.
ownership: subsidiary of Sonae SGPS
capacity_detail: Turnover EUR 1.5bn in 2025, up 7.5% (ECO News reporting Sonae results)
markets: Portugal and Spain through stores, online sales and a marketplace
rationale: Tech retailer selling gaming and electronics to young Iberians; F1 content and Madrid's new Grand Prix suit promotions.

name: Pingo Doce
desc: Portuguese supermarket chain with 497 stores, a joint venture 51% owned by Jerónimo Martins and 49% by Ahold Delhaize.
ownership: subsidiary of Jerónimo Martins (51%; Ahold Delhaize 49%)
capacity_detail: Sales EUR 5,342m in 2025, up 5.3% (Jerónimo Martins Annual Report 2025)
markets: Portugal, nationwide supermarket network
rationale: Domestic grocery brand; F1 relevance is limited to consumer promotions in Portugal.

name: LeoVegas
desc: Swedish mobile-first online casino and sports betting group, acquired by MGM Resorts International in 2022.
ownership: subsidiary of MGM Resorts International (acquired 2022, deal valued USD 607m)
capacity_detail: Official Top Sponsor of Serie A club Atalanta BC since 2021, renewed for the 2024/25 season
sponsorships: Atalanta BC Top Sponsor (2021, renewed 2024/25); Blackpool FC shirt (2023); AS Roma infotainment partner (2021)
markets: Online gaming in the Nordics, the UK, Italy, Spain and other regulated markets
rationale: Football-sponsoring betting brand whose parent MGM partners Haas; F1 content could feed its sportsbook where regulation allows.

name: Superdrug
desc: British health and beauty retailer and pharmacy chain owned by A.S. Watson, part of CK Hutchison.
ownership: subsidiary of CK Hutchison via A.S. Watson Group (AS Watson (Health & Beauty UK) Ltd)
capacity_detail: Revenue GBP 1.6bn in 2024 (Wikipedia infobox)
markets: United Kingdom and Ireland, stores, pharmacies and online
rationale: Beauty retailer targeting young UK shoppers; F1's growing female fan base could support co-branded beauty campaigns.

name: ERGO Group
desc: German primary insurance group selling life, health and property-casualty cover, wholly owned by Munich Re since 2001.
ownership: subsidiary of Munich Re (sole owner since 2001)
capacity_detail: Insurance revenue EUR 20.8bn in 2024 (Wikipedia infobox)
sponsorships: DFB Cup partner since 2016; official insurance partner of the German Football Association since 2022; national partner UEFA Euro 2024
markets: Germany and other European markets, plus international insurance operations
rationale: Heavy football sponsor seeking German brand reach; Audi's F1 entry raises German F1 interest that ERGO could use.

name: Austrian Airlines
desc: Austrian flag carrier based at Vienna International Airport, owned by Lufthansa since 2009.
ownership: subsidiary of Lufthansa Group (bought 2009; Austrian holding structure keeps 50.2% of shares in Austrian hands per Wikipedia)
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 2,541m in 2025, up 3% (Lufthansa Group Annual Report 2025)
markets: Flights from Vienna to Europe, Central and Eastern Europe, North America and Asia
rationale: Home airline for the Austrian Grand Prix at Spielberg; race-weekend travel packages and hospitality fit its Vienna hub.

name: Lufthansa Technik
desc: German aircraft maintenance, repair, overhaul and VIP completion provider, forming the Lufthansa Group's MRO segment.
ownership: subsidiary of Lufthansa Group (MRO segment)
capacity_detail: MRO segment revenue EUR 8,049m in 2025, up 12% (Lufthansa Group Annual Report 2025)
markets: Airlines and VIP aircraft owners worldwide, with stakes in 56 companies across Europe, the Americas and Asia
rationale: Engineering-led B2B brand; F1's technical image suits recruitment and VIP-completion client hospitality.

name: Lufthansa Cargo
desc: German air freight carrier and logistics specialist of the Lufthansa Group, reported as its Logistics segment.
ownership: subsidiary of Lufthansa Group (Logistics segment, Lufthansa Cargo AG)
capacity_detail: Logistics segment revenue EUR 3,403m in 2025, up 4% (Lufthansa Group Annual Report 2025)
markets: Air freight worldwide from Frankfurt, with cargo capacity on group passenger flights
rationale: F1 freight is a showcase for air cargo; a logistics partnership could demonstrate time-critical capabilities to shippers.

name: Toolstation
industry: trade tools and building supplies retailer
desc: British click-and-collect retailer of tools and building supplies for tradespeople, with stores in the UK and Benelux.
ownership: subsidiary of Travis Perkins plc
capacity_detail: Toolstation revenue GBP 843m in 2025, up 2.7% (Travis Perkins 2025 full-year results release)
markets: United Kingdom (590 stores) and the Netherlands and Belgium (109 stores)
rationale: Trade-focused brand challenging Screwfix; British GP and trades-heavy F1 audience offer brand-building, though budgets are modest.

name: Weetabix
